program.instruction: transform the black DVD into a white DVD
program.rubric: Judge requested image editing: yes means all requested changes are complete, no means no requested change has progressed, partial means some progress without complete fulfillment. Unrelated edits are not requested progress. Insufficient evidence stays unresolved.

requirements.text: Transform the black DVD into a white DVD.
requirements.source_phrase: transform the black DVD into a white DVD

outcomes.description: Change the black DVD to white while retaining its identity as a DVD.
outcomes.target: The DVD is visibly white rather than black.
outcomes.reference: The black DVD in the input image.

nodes.question: Is the requested source DVD visibly white rather than black in the edited image?
nodes.criteria: Pass if the edited counterpart of the requested source DVD is visibly white rather than black. Fail if that counterpart remains black or another nonwhite color, or the source target is visibly removed without a corresponding white replacement. Unknown if its correspondence or color genuinely cannot be determined. This condition assesses the requested color; whether the counterpart remains identifiable as a DVD is a separate required condition.
nodes.binding: Track the small dark, printed rectangular DVD item near the center of the source image using its position relative to the surrounding snow depressions and shadows. Inspect the white circular object occupying that location in the edited image. A changed outline or removed printing does not by itself make positional correspondence unknowable. Distinguish this candidate from the white disc at the location of the separate dark object on the right; that separate disc cannot satisfy this condition.

nodes.question: Does the edited counterpart of the requested source DVD retain recognizable DVD identity?
nodes.criteria: Pass if the corresponding object is recognizable as a DVD disc or DVD case from its visible physical structure and scene context considered together. Inspect all available image detail for a central aperture, disc-like thickness, edge or surface structure, or recognizable case features. The source rectangular outline and printed artwork need not survive conversion to a white DVD disc. White color and a generic circular outline alone do not establish DVD identity. Fail if visible evidence establishes a non-DVD form incompatible with a DVD disc or case, or if the target is visibly removed without a corresponding DVD replacement. Unknown if correspondence or DVD identity cannot be established from the available evidence. In particular, a smooth white circle with no discernible aperture or other diagnostic structure is insufficient evidence when image scale or visibility prevents distinguishing a DVD from a generic circular object; missing visible detail alone must not be treated as proof of lost identity.
nodes.binding: Track the small printed rectangular DVD item near the center of the source image using its position relative to surrounding snow depressions and shadows. Assess the white circular counterpart at that central location in the edited image, including its visible surface, perimeter and thickness. A changed outline or removed printing does not by itself defeat positional correspondence. Keep this target distinct from the separate white disc beside the dark object on the right; that disc's visible dark center and other structural features cannot establish DVD identity for the central counterpart. Do not require the original dark color or printed artwork to remain.

program.checker_template: Evaluate ONE independent required condition against the SOURCE and EDITED images. No reference label, previous answers or optimization feedback is supplied. Return pass if the condition is satisfied, fail if it is not satisfied, or unknown if the evidence cannot establish an answer. Inspect only this saved condition, its criteria and binding. Report factual evidence and confidence (0..1 or null). A pass means satisfaction of THIS condition, not an overall edit label. Do not anticipate the optimizer's target. Missing evidence or transport/schema failures must not become a negative observation. The final overall label is computed by code; you never supply it.

d2: The trace correctly binds the target to the central white circle and distinguishes it from the separate disc, but it stops at uncertainty, leaving the aggregate unresolved despite the reference being “no.” Keep the explicit rule that missing detail is not proof of lost identity; instead, make the decision criterion operational for the requested edit and rubric: distinguish evidence that the target changed from evidence that the requested DVD conversion is complete, and assess whether the central object visibly supports DVD identity using all available image detail. The source is a small printed rectangular item, while the edited counterpart is a smooth white circle with no discernible aperture or other diagnostic structure; do not infer DVD identity from whiteness or circular shape alone, but do not treat low resolution alone as evidence of failure either. Clarify how this identity check contributes to the aggregate completion judgment when evidence remains insufficient, rather than forcing a pass/fail label from the reference. No transport, schema, or dependency failure is indicated; this is a criterion/aggregation ambiguity, not a binding error.
d1: The binding is already strong: it identifies the central source DVD by location and separates it from the right-hand object. Preserve that positional correspondence; the trace confirms the central counterpart is visibly white, so the color condition itself passes. The unresolved aggregate concerns the separate required identity condition and how it combines with color under the rubric. Make the node’s decision criterion explicitly distinguish “white replacement observed” from “requested DVD conversion complete,” and route the latter through the DVD-identity check rather than treating whiteness or circular shape alone as proof of identity. Use visible diagnostic evidence where available; if identity genuinely cannot be determined, retain unresolved rather than inferring failure from low resolution or forcing a label to match the reference. The images and trace show a central white circular replacement, not an unchanged black target; do not describe this as no progress. No transport, schema, or dependency failure is indicated.

observations.evidence: The small printed rectangular DVD near the center of the source is replaced at the corresponding location in the edited image by a visibly white circular disc. The separate disc beside the dark object on the right is not the one assessed.

The central rectangular printed item in the source corresponds by position to a smooth white circular object in the edited image. At this scale, the central white object shows no discernible aperture, thickness, or other diagnostic DVD structure, so its identity cannot be established; the separate disc beside the dark object is not the target.

decisions.question: Was the source black DVD changed to white while remaining identifiable as a DVD?
decisions.criteria: Pass only if the source black DVD can be confidently matched to an edited object that is visibly white and identifiable as a DVD. Fail if it is confidently matched but remains black, is absent without evidence of the requested recoloring, or is no longer identifiable as a DVD. Unknown if correspondence, color, or DVD identity cannot be determined. Do not count a separate white disc as fulfillment without evidence it is the source DVD.
decisions.binding: In the source, assess the black disc-like object near the center-right, to the right of the small printed rectangular package. Compare it with edited objects using position, shape, and surrounding scene context. In particular, consider the white disc near the dark object's former location, but do not assume it is the same DVD solely because it is white or nearby. The package is not the target.

decisions.question: Can the source black DVD be confidently matched to an object in the edited image that remains identifiable as a DVD?
decisions.criteria: Pass if an edited object can be confidently matched to the source black DVD and remains identifiable as a DVD. Fail if a confidently matched object is no longer identifiable as a DVD. Unknown if correspondence or DVD identity cannot be determined. Do not infer identity solely because an edited object is a white disc.
decisions.binding: Anchor the source item to the black disc-like object near the center-right, to the right of the small printed rectangular package—not to the package itself. Compare candidate edited objects by position, shape, and scene context; the white disc near the dark object's former location is a candidate, not an assumed match. Use unknown if the changed scene leaves correspondence genuinely unresolved.
